A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original extraction experiments across open-source models, attacks on 25 customized GPTs, datastore reconstruction results, and instruction-tuning and knowledge-source ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original experiments on context size, chunking, and prompt position in Section 4.1.

M1.justification: v2 adds prompt variants that reconstruct context following an instruction or on both sides of it. These adapt the extraction procedure for positional experiments; the original open-source attack and production-GPT attack remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The Wikipedia, WikiQA, Harry Potter, and 25-GPT coverage is retained. v2 adds proof-of-concept input scenarios with instructions before or inside retrieved context, including reconstruction on both sides, extending the original end-position scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated model set and base-versus-instruction-tuned model comparisons are unchanged. Newly cited attacks are not evaluated as baselines; the added chunking comparisons are ablations of the target RAG configuration.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a character-overlap reconstruction metric and substantial new protocols: chunk-count and length sweeps, fixed-size versus sentence-boundary chunking, and prompt-position experiments including 15 insertion positions among 16 chunks. The original default hyperparameters in Table 3 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.1 retains v1's instruction-tuning and knowledge-source ablations and adds analyses of retrieval volume, fragmentation at fixed context size, semantic chunk boundaries, and positional vulnerability. Figures 3–5 substantially expand the sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain identical plus/minus reporting, and neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds. v2 Figure 5 adds shaded bands around positional curves, but their meaning and computation are undefined, preventing a reliable determination of the statistical reporting change.

E6.justification: New Mistral-Instruct-7b results show greater reconstruction with larger contexts, fewer longer chunks at fixed context size, sentence-boundary chunking, and instructions near context edges. Tables 1–2 and the headline GPT results—100% attack success and 41.73%/3.22% reconstruction—are unchanged; the additions are new-condition results.

T1.justification: Definition 1 and the autoregressive RAG formulation retain their mathematical substance, with datastore notation revised. The new context-use explanations are hypotheses, and the empirical reconstruction metric introduces no formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add RAG-configuration effects as a contribution and suggest that extraction susceptibility reflects ineffective context utilization. The central claims about datastore leakage, model scaling, instruction tuning, and production-GPT vulnerability remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations involving semantic coherence, continuation behavior, positional bias, RoPE, and causal attention. It also explicitly qualifies the positional experiments as impractical proof-of-concept settings and adds limitations concerning RIC-only coverage, automated attack design, and the absence of a defense.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code/data repository link, documents SequenceMatcher-based measurement and sentence-boundary chunking, and adds the GPT-4 anchor-query prompt in Appendix C.2. The BM25/Together AI implementation, default hyperparameters, and existing resource links are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds REPLUG and newer RAG privacy-attack citations, together with literature on long-tail knowledge, memorization, and context-position bias. These extend the existing positioning; the central novelty claim remains broadly intact, and the prompt-injection review is relocated to Appendix A.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: v1 Section 6 becomes Section 4.1 before production experiments, Disclosure moves to Broader Impact, and prompt-injection related work moves to Appendix A. The introduction and experimental exposition are expanded, setup and metrics receive clearer organization, and a Limitations section is added.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 3–5, including a two-panel positional analysis. It restyles the instruction-tuning chart and revises the reconstruction chart's legend and word-count annotations. Existing tables and appendix screenshots are retained and relocated, rather than constituting new evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 improves understanding of when extraction succeeds through controlled context-size, chunking, and positional studies, while adding explicit limitations and code/data access information. The gains are bounded: the new analyses use one Mistral model, their mechanism explanations remain hypothetical, and the plotted bands lack statistical documentation.
